messages.subject: erro copy number chrM.
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I'm using Sequenza. But something went wrong, because out.seqz.gz, only contains data regarding the chromosome (chrM).
How can I use Sequenza for all chromosomes?

I used the following command lines:

samtools faidx ./hg19.fa

sequenza-utils gc_wiggle -f ./hg19.fa -w50 | gzip > hg19.gc50Base.txt.gz

sequenza-utils bam2seqz -gc hg19.gc50Base.txt.gz -n NORMAL.sorted.bam -t TUMORAL.sorted.bam --fasta ./hg19.fa | gzip >  out.seqz.gz

sequenza-utils seqz_binning -w 50 -s out.seqz.gz | gzip > out.small.seqz.bz <http://out.small.seqz.bz>

I also tried without success:

sequenza-utils gc_wiggle -w 50 --fasta hg19.fasta -o hg19.gc50Base.wig.gz

sequenza-utils bam2seqz -n NORMAL.bam -t TUMORAL.bam --fasta hg19.fasta \
-gc hg19.gc50Base.wig.gz -o seq.gz

sequenza-utils bam2seqz -n NORMAL.bam -t TUMORAL.bam --fasta hg19.fasta -gc hg19.gc50Base.wig.gz -o seq.gz

messages.subject: Re: Sequenza on tumor only samples
messages.body_plain:
Hi Francesco,

I have a similar question/issue as someone above. I basically have WGS for the same cell line at different timepoints of treatment. I have used as normal my time 0 and I also get funny results. Also interestingly, I do get low cellularity and CNVs even if I run against this time 0 (normal) another time 0 replicate - tumour. It is basically just another subset of cells taken from the same flask - so I guess one would expect to see nothing? I was using this more of a control but it detects a lot of events.

Any advice on this analysis?

Many thanks,
Diana

Or is it better to combine the sequencing data of normal samples from multiple patients as a control?

>

>
> wupin
